question: Under what generative assumptions do co-occurrence spectra produce linear word analogies, why does PMI recover the semantic subspace at lower rank than raw co-occurrence ratios, and how robust is that explanation to noise, missing vocabulary, and removal of relation pairs?

key_findings.claim: The paper has a clean exact result for its idealized raw co-occurrence-ratio matrix: independent binary attribute factors make M a Kronecker product with analytically tractable product eigenvectors and eigenvalues.
key_findings.evidence: A vocabulary contains one word for every point of the d-dimensional binary hypercube, word marginals factor over attributes, and each attribute contributes an independent symmetric 2-by-2 context factor. Under those assumptions Equation 3 makes M(i,j)=P(i,j)/(P(i)P(j)) exactly the Kronecker product of the attribute matrices, so Equations 6–8 and the appendix product eigensystem follow. This is a useful solvable mechanism, but it is conditional on a complete Cartesian vocabulary, multiplicative context independence, positive finite factors, and consistent word ordering.

anchors.section: 5 Word embedding directly from the co-occurrence matrix

key_findings.claim: The strongest exact theorem is the affine low-rank structure of the model PMI: its nonzero column space lies in the span of the constant vector and d attribute vectors, so valid hypercube rectangles satisfy the vector parallelogram identity.
key_findings.evidence: Expanding each binary log factor gives log M = delta 11^T + A D A^T + A eta 1^T + 1 eta^T A^T. Thus rank(log M) is at most d+1 and every nonzero PMI eigenvector is affine in the attributes. Any four attribute vectors satisfying alpha_D=alpha_A-alpha_B+alpha_C consequently satisfy W_D=W_A-W_B+W_C when the retained embedding spans the needed affine directions. This identity is exact only for strictly positive factors; the empirical regularizer log(M+epsilon) no longer has the exact additive factorization.

anchors.section: 6 Word embedding from the pointwise mutual information matrix
Matrix Form, Rank and Eigenvectors, Equation 12

key_findings.claim: The synthetic model builds the desired relation into its latent representation, while the Wikipedia experiment never tests whether natural language is well described by that generative model.
key_findings.evidence: Synthetic analogies are explicitly constructed by flipping two coordinates of the same binary attribute hypercube whose PMI was proved affine in those coordinates. The Wikipedia section then compares qualitative spectral shapes and analogy curves, but never infers d, attributes, incidence probabilities, or interaction strengths; reports no likelihood or goodness-of-fit; and makes no held-out prediction against an alternative generative model. The experiments therefore validate the derivation and selected qualitative consequences, not the causal adequacy or uniqueness of binary independent attributes for real language.

anchors.section: Figure 1 and emergence of linear analogy
Numerical validation and synthetic analogy construction

key_findings.claim: The paper's PMI-to-embedding construction is mathematically inconsistent because the modeled PMI is generally indefinite and therefore cannot equal a real Gram matrix W^T W.
key_findings.evidence: In the symmetric case, each delta_k equals one half log(1-s_k^2), which is negative, while each gamma_k is positive. The constant PMI eigenvalue 2^d delta is therefore negative, not the claimed top eigenvalue, and taking its real square root in Equation 5 is impossible. For asymmetric marginals the constant and attribute basis vectors span the nonzero subspace but need not individually be eigenvectors. The paper does not specify a signed factorization, word/context SVD, PPMI projection, or negative-mode policy; the released Wikipedia code retains positive modes while synthetic code sometimes uses square roots of absolute eigenvalues.

anchors.section: A2 Coefficients characterizing the PMI matrix

key_findings.claim: Several raw-M spectral statements need additional signal-order assumptions, and one displayed singleton eigenvalue has the power of two reversed.
key_findings.evidence: Combining the product theorem with the weak-signal factor eigenvalues gives a singleton mode of order 2^(d-2) s_k(1+q_k)^2, whereas page 4 prints 2^(-(d-2)). More importantly, K at most d+1 does not guarantee that all retained nonconstant modes are single attributes: a product of strong signals can outrank a weak singleton unless explicit ordering and eigengap conditions hold. Per-factor O(s_k^2) errors also accumulate with d, so the asymptotic band argument needs a uniform condition such as sum_k s_k^2 much less than one.

key_findings.claim: The paper conflates an exact vector identity with unique top-1 completion, and its implemented Wikipedia metric does not match the metric written in the paper or used synthetically.
key_findings.evidence: Any affine projection preserves W_A-W_B+W_C=W_D even when two candidate words collide, so retrieval additionally needs injectivity, a nearest-neighbor margin, and a tie rule. The d=2,K=2 appendix actually satisfies the vector equation but cannot distinguish King from Queen, contradicting the prose that the equation is not satisfied. Equation 13 specifies raw Euclidean argmin over the full vocabulary, but the official notebook row-normalizes embeddings, applies cosine-style 3CosAdd, and excludes A, B, and C. Synthetic panels use raw Euclidean search without those exclusions, so real and synthetic curves do not share one evaluation protocol.

key_findings.claim: The Wikipedia benchmark denominator and corpus construction are materially underreported, limiting reproducibility and changing the interpretation of the reported accuracy.
key_findings.evidence: The paper says the Mikolov set has 19,544 analogies in 13 families and gives only a 10,000-word vocabulary. The official artifacts actually use the 2023-11-01 English Wikipedia dump, lowercase regex tokenization, articles with at least 500 tokens, a top-20,000 vocabulary truncated to 10,000, and a distance-weighted symmetric window of 16 over an OOV-compressed stream. Vocabulary filtering and relation-pair cross-products leave 7,614 evaluated analogies, only 39.0% of the benchmark. The source benchmark has 14 categories; adj-antonym is hidden from the per-category plot but remains in the black aggregate.

anchors.section: Data, code availability, and compute budget

key_findings.claim: The empirical smoothing choice and uncertainty display are not a clean out-of-sample validation.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 2 states log(M+epsilon_R) with epsilon=0.01 without defining R or zero-count handling. The executed reproduction notebook saves the main accuracy artifact after setting the regularizer to 0.1 and sweeps nine regularizers on the same analogy benchmark; the relation-pruning notebook uses exp(-4). The black Wikipedia curve is a micro-average over 14 categories, while its band is the unweighted sample standard deviation across 13 displayed category accuracies. That band measures category heterogeneity, is not centered on the same aggregation, and is neither a confidence interval nor corpus/seed replication.

key_findings.claim: The additive-noise section does not prove preservation of the analogy-supporting embeddings or top-1 answers.
key_findings.evidence: The argument assumes only bounded variance before invoking a Wigner spectral-norm asymptotic that needs stronger independence and tail or moment conditions. It then uses Weyl's inequality, which controls eigenvalues rather than eigenvectors, to claim that the eigendecomposition is unaffected. A valid result needs an explicit semantic eigengap, a Davis–Kahan subspace bound, and a rowwise or retrieval-margin argument. The asserted O(2^d/d) gap does not follow from nondegeneracy alone, arbitrary additive PMI noise need not correspond to a valid joint distribution, and the appendix prints a semantic-mode norm as 2^d rather than 2^(d/2), although correcting that square root recovers its final breakdown scaling.

anchors.section: 7 Additive Noise Perturbation to the PMI matrix
Breakdown of analogy accuracy with increasing K

key_findings.claim: The vocabulary-subsampling result supports robustness to uniform random missing hypercube points, not to realistic lexical sparsity, and its proof omits a coupled constant mode.
key_findings.evidence: The proof samples a uniform subset of complete hypercube rows and appeals to sample-covariance concentration when m is much greater than d. After pruning, however, the constant vector is no longer exactly orthogonal to the retained attribute columns, yet the negative delta 11^T term is dropped. Individual attribute eigenvectors also require gaps in D; without them only a subspace is identifiable. The d=12 experiment retains 15% of words, which removes about 97.75% of matrix cells, but real vocabularies are structured and frequency-biased rather than uniform random subsets of a Cartesian vocabulary.

key_findings.claim: The relation-removal experiment is a label-guided matrix-cell ablation, not removal of relation evidence from the corpus, and its degradation is not uniformly minimal.
key_findings.evidence: The formal section sets selected PMI entries to zero, which means M=1 or independence, while the prose describes deleting co-occurrences from the corpus; zero raw counts would instead give log zero and change marginals and many context pairs. The released code edits an already smoothed log matrix, assigning selected Wikipedia cells exp(-4) and synthetic cells +4, without deleting sentences, recomputing counts, or withholding indirect relation evidence. Published artifacts show the overall peak falling from 76.3% to 69.0% and city–state from 82.7% to 49.1%, although several morphology relations change little. The proof also alternates M and log M and uses Weyl to infer eigenvector stability.

anchors.section: 9 Analogy structure after removal of all pairs

key_findings.claim: The ternary and correlated-attribute appendices do not establish the broad robustness claimed in the discussion.
key_findings.evidence: For the displayed ternary matrix, B times (1,1,-2) equals three times that vector, so the new eigenvalue is 3f rather than the printed 6f; f is an interaction strength despite being called the frequency of non-neutral settings, and the new feature is not affine in the scalar ternary attribute. In the correlated extension, word-dependent normalization factors are ignored beyond first order. Their logarithms generally introduce quadratic and higher attribute features, increasing PMI rank and breaking exact parallelograms, so Equations 31–33 are at most a weak-coupling approximation rather than an exact relaxation of independence.

anchors.section: A3 Tertiary model with neutral attribute
Resulting eigenvalues of the ternary model

key_findings.claim: The empirical evidence establishes a selected spectral phenomenon, but not that trained Word2Vec or GloVe implement the paper's symmetric eigembedding or that its evaluation advantage is metric-robust.
key_findings.evidence: The only real-data comparison is raw M versus a smoothed log M positive-eigenspace construction. There is no trained Word2Vec, SGNS, or GloVe baseline; no two-matrix SVD or shifted/positive PMI control; no trivial ONLY-B or IGNORE-A baseline; no reversed analogies, 3CosMul, shuffled-pair control, alternative corpus/window/vocabulary, or pairing-consistency metric. SGNS uses separate word and context factors of shifted PMI, and GloVe uses weighted log counts plus biases, so neither is the symmetric W^T W construction evaluated here.

key_findings.claim: The paper's narrow novelty is real: it unifies finite-rank emergence, raw-M versus PMI behavior, and several perturbations in one solvable attribute model, but it is not the first probabilistic, PMI, spectral, or co-occurrence explanation of analogies.
key_findings.evidence: The closest same-group predecessor already explains sequential spectral learning and analogy emergence; Torii et al. already connect co-occurrence symmetries to parallelograms; Arora et al., Gittens et al., Allen and Hospedales, and Ethayarajh et al. give earlier generative or PMI explanations. The target contributes an upstream binary-attribute mechanism with exact raw-M and PMI structure and an integrated perturbation program. Its bibliography also miscites Ethayarajh, Duvenaud, and Hirst as Ethayarajh, Jurafsky, and Krishna and omits several direct analogy-evaluation critiques.

anchors.section: Related Work and proposed attribute view

method.core_idea: Represent every word as a binary semantic-attribute vector, factor word and context statistics independently across attributes, derive the spectra of the resulting co-occurrence-ratio and PMI matrices, and examine when truncated spectral embeddings preserve attribute rectangles as word analogies.
method.mechanism: The complete binary vocabulary creates a d-fold Kronecker product for M, whose eigenvectors are products of constant and contrast modes. Weak, similarly sized signals place the single-attribute modes near the top, so low-dimensional raw-M embeddings become affine in selected attributes; higher-order product modes can later disrupt retrieval. Taking log turns the product into a sum and confines PMI to the span of the constant and d attribute columns, making valid attribute rectangles exact when their directions are represented. Random additive noise, uniform vocabulary thinning, and selected relation-cell edits are then treated as spectral perturbations, and analogy top-1 accuracy is compared on synthetic hypercubes and one Wikipedia co-occurrence pipeline.
assumptions: Every one of the 2^d binary attribute combinations initially corresponds to a word.
Attribute incidences factor across a word and each attribute independently affects word-context co-occurrence.
Each per-attribute context matrix is symmetric, marginal-compatible, positively associated, and strictly positive wherever PMI is taken.
Semantic strengths are nonzero and sufficiently separated for the desired attribute modes and retrieval candidates to be identifiable.
Weak-signal expansions remain uniform as d grows and product modes do not interleave before required singleton modes.
A symmetric eigenembedding of M or PMI is an informative surrogate for trained Word2Vec and GloVe despite their different objectives and word/context factors.
Negative PMI eigenvalues can be omitted or otherwise handled without changing the semantic conclusion.
Exact affine vector identities imply unique nearest-neighbor completion once the relevant directions are retained.
Additive symmetric entry noise has suitable tails, independence, eigengaps, and a magnitude that preserves the semantic invariant subspace.
Uniform random vocabulary subsampling approximates the structured and frequency-biased missingness of real vocabularies.
Editing selected entries of a smoothed PMI matrix is a meaningful proxy for removing relation evidence from a corpus.
Weak correlated-attribute corrections and a ternary attribute construction preserve the same affine structure beyond their leading-order calculations.
One English Wikipedia preprocessing configuration and one analogy probe are sufficient qualitative evidence for the proposed natural-language mechanism.

techniques.role: Assigns each word a vector in {−1,+1}^d and defines analogy tuples as two-coordinate rectangles.
Builds word marginals and context interactions as products of independent per-attribute terms.
Obtains the complete raw-M spectrum from tensor products of 2-by-2 attribute eigenvectors.
Orders constant, singleton-attribute, and higher-order attribute-product modes through small-s expansions.
Turns multiplicative attribute factors into a constant, linear marginal terms, and an attribute bilinear form.
Uses the span of one and the attribute matrix to prove rank at most d+1 and exact vector parallelograms.
Varies embedding dimension K to compare when raw M and smoothed PMI support analogy retrieval.
Enumerates hypercube rectangles and scores raw-Euclidean top-1 completion.
Constructs a 10,000-word weighted context matrix from English Wikipedia and evaluates a normalized spectral representation.
Perturbs synthetic PMI entries and tracks semantic/noise spectral mixing and analogy breakdown.
Randomly retains a fraction of hypercube words and compares the thinned Gram spectrum and analogy accuracy.
Edits smoothed log-matrix entries corresponding to known relation pairs and reevaluates the same relation categories.
Sketches neutral attribute states and weak cross-attribute interactions as robustness extensions.

evaluations.setting: English Wikipedia co-occurrence matrices with a displayed 10,000-word vocabulary and the Mikolov analogy benchmark.
evaluations.metric: Eigenvalue spectrum and analogy top-1 accuracy as embedding dimension K increases.
evaluations.result: Smoothed log M generally scores above raw M and saturates over a broad K range, while raw M peaks and can degrade. Artifact inspection shows that the implemented normalized 3CosAdd score covers 7,614 filtered analogies rather than all 19,544.
evaluations.baseline: A spectral embedding of the unsmoothed raw co-occurrence-ratio matrix M.

evaluations.setting: Complete symmetric binary hypercubes with d=8 and semantic strengths drawn from narrow or broad distributions over repeated realizations.
evaluations.metric: Raw-Euclidean top-1 accuracy on all two-attribute rectangle completions versus K.
evaluations.result: Raw M gives band-dependent accuracy when strengths are narrow and loses exact completion when higher-order modes interleave under broad strengths; the synthetic log M reaches 100% once the semantic directions are present.
evaluations.baseline: The exact attribute rectangle and the alternative raw-M or log-M spectral target.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic d=8 PMI matrices with multiplicative probability noise, equivalent to additive Gaussian log-matrix noise, over ten reported realizations.
evaluations.metric: Analogy accuracy across embedding dimension, noise scale, and rescaled K.
evaluations.result: Accuracy remains high through a low-rank region and eventually falls as noisy eigenvectors enter; the appendix reports a collapse near K proportional to 2^(d/2)/sigma after correcting a normalization slip.
evaluations.baseline: The unperturbed synthetic PMI spectrum and analogy curve.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic d=12 vocabularies retaining a random fraction f=0.15 of hypercube words, with additional multiplicative noise.
evaluations.metric: Leading semantic eigenvalues and analogy accuracy after rescaling by the retained fraction.
evaluations.result: The selected trials preserve leading semantic modes and reach high analogy accuracy when m is well above d. The text describes more than 97% of the matrix removed, corresponding to 85% of words but roughly 97.75% of cells.

evaluations.setting: Wikipedia smoothed-log matrices with benchmark relation-pair cells jointly edited, then evaluated on the same relation-labeled analogies.
evaluations.metric: Peak normalized 3CosAdd accuracy by category and overall.
evaluations.result: Several morphology categories remain relatively stable, but published artifacts show overall peak accuracy decreasing from 0.763 to 0.690 and city–state from 0.827 to 0.491, so degradation is category-dependent rather than uniformly minimal.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic d=8 log matrices with entries for the strongest or weakest attribute relation edited over ten semantic-strength realizations.
evaluations.metric: Top-1 accuracy for analogies involving the edited attribute versus other attributes across K.
evaluations.result: Both groups can return to perfect accuracy at K=d and later degrade as perturbation modes enter, demonstrating redundant indirect structure in this constructed model.
evaluations.baseline: Analogies in dimensions whose direct cells were not edited and the unperturbed model.

evaluations.setting: Raw-M spectrum simulations at d=8 with 50 semantic-strength realizations spanning narrow Gaussian and uniform distributions.
evaluations.metric: Spectral density and analogy accuracy at complete eigenband boundaries.
evaluations.result: Narrow strengths reveal constant, singleton, and product bands with perfect accuracy at complete bands; broader strengths merge the bands into an approximately log-normal-looking spectrum and create nonmonotone accuracy.
evaluations.baseline: The empirical Wikipedia spectrum shown on the same figure and alternative strength distributions.

evaluations.setting: One released implementation and notebook suite linked by the paper.
evaluations.metric: Agreement between stated and executable corpus, factorization, smoothing, pruning, and analogy procedures.
evaluations.result: The code reveals useful details and fixed seeds but differs from the paper in metric, source-word exclusion, denominator, smoothing, negative-mode handling, sparse-noise value, and relation-cell edit. Several large intermediate artifacts are absent, so a fresh clone is not fully end-to-end reproducible.
evaluations.baseline: Equations 5, 13–14 and Figures 2–3 as described in the PDF.

limitations: Reviewer inference: the complete binary hypercube assumes all Cartesian attribute combinations exist and excludes polysemy, graded features, hierarchy, context dependence, and lexical gaps.
Reviewer inference: independent attribute factors make the PMI affine by construction, so synthetic exact analogy accuracy is not an independent test of the explanatory mechanism.
Reviewer inference: Wikipedia attributes and generative parameters are never inferred, and no likelihood, goodness-of-fit, held-out prediction, or alternative generative model is evaluated.
Contradiction audit: the modeled PMI is indefinite, so it cannot equal a real W^T W Gram matrix and its negative-eigenvalue policy is unstated and inconsistent across code paths.
Contradiction audit: the displayed raw-M singleton eigenvalue has 2^(-(d-2)) where the product theorem gives 2^(d-2).
Reviewer inference: weak-signal band ordering needs uniform remainder bounds, nonzero signals, and explicit mode-separation assumptions not supplied by K at most d+1.
Reviewer inference: affine vector equality is weaker than unique nearest-neighbor retrieval and requires a tie rule and a quantitative candidate margin.
Contradiction audit: Equation 13, the Wikipedia notebook, and the synthetic notebook use different normalization and source-word-exclusion rules.
Contradiction audit: only 7,614 filtered analogy tuples are evaluated, while the paper presents the full 19,544 count and misstates the benchmark as 13 rather than 14 categories.
Reviewer inference: category standard deviation is not uncertainty across corpora, seeds, preprocessing pipelines, or sampling of analogy tuples.
Reviewer inference: smoothing is incompletely defined, inconsistent between caption and artifacts, and exposed to selection on the same analogy benchmark.
Reviewer inference: the perturbation proof uses eigenvalue stability where eigenvector, rowwise, and retrieval-margin stability are required.
Reviewer inference: uniform random vocabulary thinning does not model frequency- and semantics-dependent lexical missingness.
Contradiction audit: relation removal edits selected smoothed PMI entries rather than removing corpus sentences or counts and recomputing marginals.
Contradiction audit: the ternary eigenvalue has a factor-of-two error and the correlated-attribute argument is only first-order despite an exact-sounding conclusion.
Reviewer inference: trained SGNS, Word2Vec, and GloVe are not evaluated, and their objectives differ materially from symmetric eigendecomposition.
Reviewer inference: no cross-corpus, cross-language, alternate-window, vocabulary-size, tokenization, finite-count, or real-noise robustness study is reported.
Author acknowledged: polysemy and hierarchical attributes remain outside the model and motivate richer future generative theories.
failure_modes: A necessary attribute combination is absent or systematically rare, so a relation is not a complete affine rectangle and top-1 completion has no valid target.
Attribute effects interact or depend on context strongly enough that log normalizers introduce higher-order features outside span{1,A}.
A weak singleton attribute is outranked by products of stronger attributes in raw M, causing higher-order modes to enter before the needed semantic direction.
PMI has large negative semantic modes, and discarding them in a positive Gram projection removes relation information.
Several words collide in a truncated affine projection, making exact vector arithmetic compatible with multiple nearest neighbors and order-dependent ties.
Frequency-weighted corpus noise is heteroskedastic, correlated, and heavy-tailed, violating the iid homoskedastic Wigner perturbation model.
Semantic eigengaps shrink with dimension or signals cluster, so a small operator perturbation rotates individual directions substantially.
Vocabulary missingness is biased by morphology, frequency, or semantic feasibility rather than uniform over a hypercube, distorting the retained Gram matrix.
A smoothing constant or zero-count rule creates artificial low-rank structure or changes eigenvalue order, and the chosen value is tuned to the evaluation set.
Changing from Euclidean to cosine retrieval, excluding source words, or altering normalization reverses the apparent K at which an analogy emerges.
An aggregate top-1 score is driven by large easy morphology categories while small semantic categories fail completely.
Editing only labeled relation cells leaves indirect and unlabeled relation evidence intact, so apparent zero-shot recovery does not survive actual corpus-level removal.
A trained SGNS or GloVe model weights, shifts, or separates word/context factors in a way that does not preserve the symmetric PMI eigenvectors.
The relation is contextual, asymmetric, hierarchical, many-to-many, or non-affine, so a single global offset is the wrong object.
reusable_insights: A multiplicative latent-factor model becomes an additive low-rank model after taking logs; this is a broadly useful route to solvable representation geometry.
Separate exact vector identities, subspace recovery, and unique retrieval accuracy: each requires a different theorem and validation metric.
For an indefinite similarity matrix, state whether the representation uses a signed factorization, two-sided SVD, positive projection, or absolute eigenvalues before interpreting geometry.
Spectral robustness claims should proceed from an operator-norm bound to an invariant-subspace bound and finally to a rowwise or nearest-neighbor margin bound.
A synthetic task generated from the same coordinates that define the theorem is a unit test, not evidence that those coordinates explain real data.
Fit latent generative parameters and test held-out co-occurrence statistics if a qualitative spectrum match is being used to claim predictive power.
Report the post-filtering benchmark denominator and per-category survival because vocabulary truncation can change both difficulty and category weights.
Keep aggregation and uncertainty aligned: micro-averages, macro-averages, category dispersion, seed variance, and confidence intervals answer different questions.
Analogy evaluation should include source-exclusion and normalization ablations plus trivial, reversed, shuffled-pair, and offset-consistency controls.
Corpus-level deletion, count-matrix deletion, PMI-zeroing, and label-held-out evaluation are distinct interventions and should never share one label.
Random feature or vocabulary pruning establishes robustness to random missingness only; realistic structured missingness needs its own model and tests.
Compare an analytic corpus-matrix surrogate with the actual learning objectives and factorizations of the algorithms invoked in the motivation.
A model can make a valuable mechanistic contribution even when its empirical fit is weak; phrase novelty around the solved mechanism rather than universal causality.
Release the exact artifact-generating configuration, not only a notebook, when captions depend on smoothing, seeds, preprocessing, and hidden intermediate files.
open_questions: Can binary or graded semantic attributes be inferred from real co-occurrence matrices and evaluated by held-out likelihood rather than selected analogy curves?
What identifiable generative alternatives produce the same rank-d affine PMI structure, and which corpus statistics distinguish them?
How do negative PMI eigenmodes contribute to analogies under signed factorizations, word/context SVD, SGNS, GloVe, and PPMI?
What explicit eigengap and nearest-neighbor margin conditions are sufficient for top-1 analogy stability under finite-sample corpus noise?
Can heteroskedastic count noise and marginal-estimation error yield realistic nonasymptotic subspace and retrieval bounds?
Does raw-M band emergence persist after correcting the singleton eigenvalue formula and enforcing uniform weak-signal remainder bounds?
How often do real analogy families correspond to valid Cartesian attribute rectangles rather than approximate, contextual, or many-to-many relations?
Do conclusions survive standard 3CosAdd, Euclidean, 3CosMul, pairing-consistency, and normalized residual metrics under one preregistered protocol?
How much of the reported Wikipedia gain remains after ONLY-B, IGNORE-A, reversal, shuffled-pair, relation-mean, and source-exclusion controls?
Does the PMI-versus-M pattern replicate across languages, domains, Wikipedia dumps, context definitions, vocabulary sizes, and tokenization pipelines?
What happens when vocabulary gaps are sampled from frequency- and semantics-dependent mechanisms rather than uniformly from a hypercube?
Can a true corpus-level relation deletion with counts and marginals recomputed reproduce the post-hoc matrix-cell result?
How should neutral, hierarchical, correlated, and polysemous attributes be modeled while retaining a tractable but non-baked-in analogy prediction?
Can trained Word2Vec and GloVe dynamics recover the same attribute subspace, including the timing and ordering of relation emergence?
Can a model predict in advance which analogy categories emerge at which K, rather than fitting only the aggregate qualitative curve?
What is the smallest end-to-end corpus artifact and deterministic pipeline needed to reproduce every reported figure from a fresh clone?

competitive_landscape.title: Closed-Form Training Dynamics Reveal Learned Features and Linear Structure in Word2Vec-like Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Karkada et al. analyze a quadratic Word2Vec-like surrogate whose training sequentially learns corpus-matrix eigenspaces and predicts when analogy behavior emerges. The target moves upstream to propose why the corpus matrices have attribute eigenvectors and why log M differs from raw M, but it relies on the predecessor for the training-dynamics connection.

competitive_landscape.title: A Latent Variable Model Approach to PMI-based Word Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: Arora et al. derive PMI inner products and analogy structure from a latent discourse random-walk model plus near-isotropy. The target replaces exogenous Euclidean latent vectors and spherical assumptions with discrete attributes of unequal strength, producing a broad semantic spectrum and exact affine rank bound, but it does not fit its alternative model to data.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Understanding Linear Word Analogies
competitive_landscape.difference: Ethayarajh, Duvenaud, and Hirst characterize when perfectly reconstructed SGNS or GloVe spaces support a linear analogy through equality of shifted PMI or conditional-probability structure. The target proposes a generative reason that such ratios can agree and studies spectral truncation, but it miscites this paper's coauthors and does not reconcile its symmetric indefinite factorization with the algorithms analyzed there.

competitive_landscape.title: Analogies Explained: Towards Understanding Word Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: Allen and Hospedales derive linear relations from probabilistic paraphrases and transformations and expose error terms in PMI-factorizing embeddings. The target substitutes independent attribute interactions and predicts eigenvalue ordering and perturbation behavior; it does not test the two mechanisms against each other on held-out corpus statistics.

competitive_landscape.title: Skip-Gram − Zipf + Uniform = Vector Additivity
competitive_landscape.difference: Gittens, Achlioptas, and Mahoney prove additive compositionality and analogy arithmetic under explicit corpus-generation assumptions and derive a nonlinear correction when those assumptions fail. The target allows unequal attribute strengths and focuses on raw-M versus PMI eigenbands, offering a different mechanism rather than the first generative explanation of additivity.

competitive_landscape.title: Neural Word Embedding as Implicit Matrix Factorization
competitive_landscape.difference: Levy and Goldberg show that SGNS factorizes shifted PMI with separate word and context embeddings and compare explicit SPPMI/SVD variants on analogy tasks. The target supplies a latent semantic mechanism for why a PMI matrix can contain affine directions, but its symmetric W^T W construction is not the SGNS factorization established by this predecessor.

competitive_landscape.title: Word Embeddings as Metric Recovery in Semantic Spaces
competitive_landscape.difference: Hashimoto, Alvarez-Melis, and Jaakkola view log co-occurrence from random walks as recovery of a latent Euclidean semantic metric or manifold. The target rejects an unconstrained Euclidean latent geometry in favor of explicit binary attributes and studies which spectral dimensions yield analogies, at the cost of a much more Cartesian semantic space.

competitive_landscape.title: Analogies minus analogy test
competitive_landscape.difference: Fournier, Dupoux, and Dunbar show that arithmetic retrieval conflates offset concentration, within-pair similarity, and genuine pairing consistency, then propose decomposed diagnostics. The target's top-1 curves therefore do not by themselves validate parallelogram structure; normalized residuals, shuffled-pair controls, offset concentration, and pairing consistency would test the claimed geometry more directly.

competitive_landscape.title: Bidirectional Attention as a Mixture of Continuous Word Experts
competitive_landscape.relationship: uncited extension to CBOW and attention
competitive_landscape.difference: Wibisono and Wang interpret CBOW and bidirectional attention as mixtures of continuous word experts and characterize conditions for their embeddings to display analogies, finding stronger requirements for attention. It is the most direct missing bridge to contextual models; the target's discussion suggests LLM relevance without showing that its static attribute-PMI mechanism survives attention.

competitive_landscape.title: Linguistic Regularities in Continuous Space Word Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Mikolov, Yih, and Zweig introduce the vector-offset regularities and benchmark family that motivate the target. The target seeks a spectral generative explanation, but its filtered 7,614-tuple implementation and altered category accounting mean the empirical score is not directly the complete benchmark presented in this predecessor.

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding the Source of Semantic Regularities in Word Embeddings
competitive_landscape.difference: Chiang, Camacho-Collados, and Pardos remove relation-bearing sentences or word pairs at the corpus level and retrain embeddings to study indirect evidence. The target analytically motivates redundancy, but its released experiment merely edits labeled cells of a smoothed log matrix and therefore is a weaker, non-equivalent intervention.

competitive_landscape.title: Issues in Evaluating Semantic Spaces Using Word Analogies
competitive_landscape.difference: Linzen shows that analogy accuracy is affected by category imbalance, trivial vector baselines, reversal, and query construction, and documents the benchmark's 14 categories. The target reports a micro-aggregate and category dispersion without these controls and incorrectly describes the source benchmark as 13 families.

competitive_landscape.title: The (Too Many) Problems of Analogical Reasoning with Word Vectors
competitive_landscape.difference: Rogers, Drozd, and Li catalog semantic, linguistic, and evaluation problems with the standard offset task and show that many reported regularities are fragile. The target's exact synthetic rectangles avoid some semantic ambiguity, but its Wikipedia validation inherits the benchmark issues and does not use a broader analogy resource or multiple retrieval methods.

competitive_landscape.title: The Word Analogy Testing Caveat
competitive_landscape.difference: Schluter demonstrates that normalized vector-offset testing and exclusion of source words can create or inflate apparent analogy structure. This is directly relevant because the target's paper writes raw Euclidean search while its Wikipedia code normalizes and excludes all three query words, with no ablation.

competitive_landscape.title: Word Embeddings, Analogies, and Machine Learning: Beyond king - man + woman = queen
competitive_landscape.difference: Drozd, Gladkova, and Matsuoka show that the analogy-retrieval algorithm itself materially changes results and propose relation-learning alternatives beyond a fixed 3CosAdd offset. The target attributes its K-curves to spectral content without testing whether the emergence point and category ranking persist under alternative solvers.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Origins of Linear Representations in Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: competing explanatory locus for modern linearity
competitive_landscape.difference: Jiang et al. use a latent next-token model to attribute linear representation to the prediction objective and gradient descent's implicit bias. The target instead locates the mechanism in static corpus statistics before training. The two accounts concern different representation settings, and the target does not empirically establish its proposed transfer from static PMI to contextual LLM activations.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims an analytically solvable generative account that explains why analogy-supporting directions appear among leading co-occurrence eigenvectors, why PMI is better behaved than raw M, how accuracy changes with embedding dimension, and why analogies survive noise, missing words, correlations, and removal of direct relation pairs.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The binary attribute factorization yields an exact Kronecker eigensystem for raw M and an exact rank-at-most-d+1 affine form for PMI, then places noise, vocabulary thinning, and relation-cell perturbations in the same spectral framework. Synthetic and Wikipedia figures reproduce several selected qualitative curves.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The integrated mechanism is a worthwhile and apparently novel synthesis relative to the checked primary literature, especially the contrast between product modes in M and additive attribute modes in PMI. It is not the first co-occurrence, probabilistic, PMI, spectral, or generative explanation of analogies, and several robustness claims exceed their proofs or implementations. The durable novelty is the solvable binary-attribute spectral model and its testable finite-rank predictions, not a validated causal model of natural language or a theorem about trained Word2Vec, GloVe, attention, or LLM representations.

reviewer_notes: Primary full-text review covered all 21 extracted pages, including every appendix. Three independent passes audited the mathematics, empirical artifacts, and current competitive literature. Competitive checks used only arXiv, ACL Anthology, PMLR, NeurIPS proceedings, and the publisher record through 2026-08-23. The official reproduction repository and artifact notebooks were inspected to resolve implementation details; these reveal metric, denominator, smoothing, negative-mode, pruning, and preprocessing choices absent from or inconsistent with the PDF. Numerical paper results are identified as author-reported, code-artifact discrepancies as contradiction audits, and causal or generalization boundaries as reviewer inference.
